description:
Are you team folded collar or funnel neck on your sweaters? #knitting ##knittok##stepbystepsweater##knitsweater
Compare folded collars and funnel necks on the Step by Step Sweater by Florence. Pros, look differences, and which style to choose. #knitting #knittok #stepbystepsweater #knitsweater
Are you team folded collar or funnel neck on your sweaters? This quick guide compares the folded collar and the funnel neck as applied to the Step by Step Sweater by Florence so you can decide which finish suits your project and personal style.

Quick comparison
- Folded collar: A turned-over neckline that reads classic and finished. Adds structure and frames the face. Works well when you want a neat, wearable edge and a traditional sweater silhouette.
- Funnel neck: A higher, unturned neckline that forms a short tube around the neck. Offers extra warmth and a modern, streamlined look. Better when you want coverage without a bulky fold.

How each affects the Step by Step Sweater by Florence
- Folded collar on this pattern preserves the sweater’s original relaxed shape while giving a clear, polished edge. It’s ideal if you prefer a softer neck height and a slightly dressier appearance.
- Funnel neck emphasizes warmth and contemporary style. On Florence’s Step by Step Sweater it creates a cozy, sweater-forward statement and pairs well with casual layering.

Style tips
- Choose folded collar if you want: a classic finish, easier layering under jackets, and a face-framing neckline.
- Choose funnel neck if you want: added warmth, a minimalist aesthetic, and less fuss about a turned hem.

Practical considerations
- Yarn weight and drape: Bulky yarns can make a folded collar heavy; a funnel neck may be neater with thicker yarn. Lightweight yarns will let a folded collar fold crisply.
- Neck circumference: Ensure the collar (folded or funnel) has comfortable ease — test on a swatch before finishing.
- Blocking and finishing: Folded collars often need careful blocking and even seaming to sit right; funnel necks rely more on consistent stitch tension.

Final takeaway
Both collars work well on the Step by Step Sweater by Florence. Pick folded collar for a classic, framed look; pick funnel neck for warmth and a modern silhouette. Which are you—team folded collar or team funnel neck?

Lead
Long skirts are adorable and versatile—especially plaid maxi skirts. This guide shows practical, easy outfit ideas to wear a long skirt for everyday style while keeping the look cute and effortless.

Body
Why choose a plaid maxi skirt
- Plaid adds visual interest without heavy effort, making a long skirt feel both classic and playful.
- Maxi length gives coverage and comfort while allowing for layering and varied shoe choices.

Simple styling ideas
1. Casual tee + maxi skirt
- Pair a fitted or slightly oversized tee tucked at the front to define the waist. Add sneakers or ankle boots for a relaxed, cute look.

2. Sweater + skirt for cooler days
- A cropped sweater or a sweater tucked loosely into the waistband keeps proportions balanced. Choose neutral tones if the plaid is bold.

3. Layered with jacket
- Denim or leather jackets add structure. For a softer look, try a cardigan or long coat that follows the skirt’s line.

4. Belt and accessories
- A simple belt emphasizes the waist on fuller skirts. Minimal jewelry and a crossbody bag keep the outfit light and wearable.

5. Shoes to match the mood
- Sneakers for casual days, ankle boots for edge, or flats and loafers for a polished look. Heels can dress the plaid maxi up for evening wear.

Fabric and fit tips
- Lightweight fabrics work for flowy movement; sturdier fabrics hold shape and suit structured tops.
- If the skirt is high-waisted, pair with cropped tops or tuck-ins. Mid or low-rise skirts pair well with longer tops or layered jackets.

Closing / Takeaway
Long plaid skirts are a simple way to create cute, adaptable outfits. Start with a basic tee or sweater, add a jacket or belt as needed, and pick shoes that match your day. Which maxi skirt look will you try first? Share your favorite styling tip or outfit combination.

Body
- Choose your silhouette: A-line plaid skirts give a classic, flattering shape; pleated plaid skirts create a preppy or schoolgirl vibe; skorts offer the same plaid aesthetic with added comfort and mobility.

- Top pairings: For a casual everyday look, pair a plaid skirt with a fitted tee, tucked-in blouse, or a cropped sweater. To make the outfit dressier, swap for a button-up shirt or a lightweight knit tucked at the waist.

- Layering and outerwear: Add a denim jacket or leather jacket for edge, or a blazer for polish. In cooler weather, layer tights or knee-high socks with ankle boots or loafers.

- Footwear choices: Sneakers keep the look relaxed; ankle boots or Chelsea boots add autumnal flair; ballet flats or loafers reinforce a preppy mood. Heels or block sandals lift a dressier plaid skirt outfit.

- Color and pattern balance: If the plaid skirt has bold colors, keep the rest of the outfit neutral. For muted plaid, experiment with color-blocking tops or textured knits.

- Styling a skort: Treat a plaid skort like a skirt but prioritize comfort—pair with fitted tops to balance the fuller bottom and choose flats or low heels for easy movement.

Close

A little bit of late summer wearable whimsy inspo. How to style a plaid maxi skirt 4 ways. Which one is your favorite?
4 whimsical ways to wear a plaid maxi skirt this late summer—casual, layered, dressy, and cozy looks with styling tips. 🤎🌿🍂✨
Lead
A little late-summer wearable whimsy: four distinct ways to style a plaid maxi skirt so it feels fresh, versatile, and season-appropriate. These looks show how one skirt can move from casual to dressy while keeping subtle, playful details.

Body
1) Casual Everyday
Start with a simple fitted tee or a lightweight ribbed tank tucked into the plaid maxi skirt. Add low-profile sneakers or flat sandals and a crossbody bag for hands-free ease. Keep jewelry minimal—small hoops or a delicate pendant—to preserve that effortless vibe.

Why it works: The tucked top balances the skirt’s volume and keeps the silhouette streamlined for daytime errands or coffee dates.

2) Layered & Earthy
Layer a cropped knit or a boxy cardigan over a tucked camisole, or drape an unbuttoned utility shirt for texture. Choose warm, earthy accessories—leather ankle boots, a braided belt, and a neutral tote. Introduce a lightweight scarf or a suede hat for extra late-summer warmth.

Why it works: Layering adds dimension and brings out the skirt’s color palette, creating a nature-inspired, wearable outfit for cooler evenings.

3) Dressy Whimsy
Swap to a fitted blouse or a silky camisole and add a tailored blazer or a cropped jacket. Elevate with heeled mules or strappy sandals and statement earrings. A compact clutch and a subtle belt at the waist make the silhouette polished without losing the skirt’s playful pattern.

Why it works: Mixing structured pieces and delicate accessories transforms the skirt into a refined look suitable for dinners or small events.

4) Cozy Transitional Look
Pair the plaid maxi with an oversized sweater half-tucked at the front. Choose chunky boots or platform loafers and layer with opaque tights if needed. Finish with a soft beanie or a slouchy beret for whimsical charm.

Why it works: The contrast between an oversized top and the long skirt creates a relaxed, fashion-forward balance that’s perfect as summer shifts into fall.

Close / Takeaway
A plaid maxi skirt is a versatile wardrobe cornerstone: tuck and pair for casual days, layer earth tones for late-summer warmth, add structure for dressier moments, or cozy up with oversized knits for transitional weather. Which outfit feels most like you? Try each variation and adapt fabrics and accessories to your climate and personal style. 🤎🌿🍂✨

Fall mini skirt set plaid • small 170lbs 5’3 #falloutfits #skirtset #miniskirt 
Styling a plaid fall mini skirt set for petite plus-size (5'3", 170lbs): fit tips, layering ideas, and shoe pairings to flatter your shape. #falloutfits #skirtset #miniskirt
Lead
A fall plaid mini skirt set can be a confident, seasonal look for someone who is petite and curvy. This guide focuses on styling a plaid skirt-and-top set when you’re about 5'3" and around 170 lbs, offering practical fit, layering, and footwear suggestions that flatter your proportions while keeping cozy for autumn.

Body
1. Choose the right fit
- Waist and hips: Look for a skirt with a defined waistband or slight stretch to sit comfortably at your natural waist. Avoid extremely tight cuts that create pulling at buttons or seams. A-line or slightly flared minis balance hips and create a smoother silhouette.
- Top length: For a set, pick a top that either ends at the waistband or is slightly cropped. If the top is longer, consider tucking or half-tucking to preserve waist definition.

2. Layering for warmth and proportion
- Lightweight tights or ribbed tights add warmth and elongate legs visually. Dark, matte tights work best for a streamlined look.
- Add a fitted cardigan, cropped jacket, or blazer that hits at or just above the waistband to maintain proportion. Longer coats can work if you keep the skirt visible and add heels or booties to lengthen the leg line.
- Scarves and hats: A slim scarf or beret draws the eye upward without adding bulk.

3. Shoe pairings
- Ankle boots or heeled booties create vertical lift and complement minis. Choose a heel height you can walk in comfortably.
- Knee-high or over-the-knee boots can also work; select a close-fitting shaft to avoid bunching and visual shortening.
- For a casual vibe, pair with loafers and opaque tights.

4. Accessories and finishing touches
- Belts: A narrow to medium belt at the waist can emphasize curves and create an hourglass effect.
- Jewelry: Keep necklaces simple to avoid competing with plaid; stud earrings or a small pendant work well.
- Bag: A crossbody or structured small tote balances the look without overwhelming a petite frame.

5. Practical outfit combinations
- Daytime casual: Plaid mini skirt set + ribbed tights + flat ankle boots + cropped denim jacket.
- Elevated day: Set with fitted blazer, heeled booties, and narrow belt.
- Cozy evening: Add knee-high boots, wool coat that ends above the knee, and a slim scarf.

Close / Call-to-action
Experiment with proportions to find what feels comfortable and confident—small adjustments like choosing the right tights, jacket length, or heel height make a noticeable difference.
